idiom_name: sequence identifier + position + size/end marker in message metadata, with a per-sequence reassembly buffer
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: split the payload or batch, then stamp every part with three fields in the message metadata - a sequence identifier that separates this group from others, a 1-based position that orders it within the group, and a size or end marker that says when the group is complete. The receiver keeps one buffer per sequence identifier, stores parts by position, ignores duplicates and releases the group in position order only after the size or end marker has been seen (or a timeout closes the group as partial). Prefer the platform's grouping feature where one exists (broker message groups, sessions, framework aggregator/resequencer) and hand-roll the header protocol only where the transport offers nothing. Acknowledge or commit only after the whole group has been released, so a crash re-delivers the batch instead of losing it.
code_sketch:
send: for pos, part in enumerate(parts, start=1):
          publish(body=part,
                  headers={SequenceId: gid, Position: pos, Size: len(parts)})
recv: g = buffers.get(SequenceId) or new_group(Size)
      g[Position] = body
      if g.is_complete(): deliver(g.in_position_order()); release(SequenceId)
pitfalls: Omitting the sequence identifier: two groups from the same sender interleave into one corrupt buffer.
Waiting for a missing part without an expiry: the group holds its buffer forever.
Trusting the channel's order: position numbers exist precisely because the channel may reorder or drop parts.

Wrong move: Treating JMSXGroupID or an Azure Service Bus session as the complete Message Sequence protocol -> broker ordering alone does not signal a missing fragment or reassemble an oversized payload -> instead carry an explicit position plus size/end marker, or use Claim Check when fragmentation is avoidable.

Wrong move: Hashing related Kafka records to a key and assuming that creates global order -> Kafka preserves order only within each partition, so records spread across keys or partitions can interleave -> instead keep one sequence on one partition or reassemble by sequence metadata before domain processing.

Wrong move: Using a timeout as the completion condition -> a quiet or delayed channel can expire a still-incomplete group and release corrupted data -> instead require the declared size or last marker, and use timeout only to route partial groups to retry or dead letter.
